subject: ent
title: Dysphagia and the oesophagus

steps.tx: Dysphagia splits into oropharyngeal transfer failure with coughing, choking, nasal regurgitation and recurrent pneumonia seconds after the attempt, versus oesophageal transit failure with food sticking retrosternally seconds later. Stroke, Parkinson disease, motor neuron disease and structural Zenker or cricopharyngeal causes drive transfer failure, while solids only progression suggests mechanical **stricture** or cancer and solids with liquids from onset suggests **achalasia**. Atopic young adults with intermittent solid impaction raise eosinophilic **oesophagitis** until scoped.
steps.say: Timing and pattern separate the two levels of dysphagia. Coughing, choking and nasal escape immediately on swallowing are markers of transfer failure. Sticking behind the sternum seconds later is a marker of oesophageal disease. Solids only progression suggests stricture or cancer while both solids and liquids from onset suggest motility failure. Young atopic impaction is typically eosinophilic disease.

vis.caption: Differentiating oropharyngeal (transfer) and oesophageal (transit) dysphagia

steps.tx: Alarm features override functional labels at any age, including progressive course, weight loss, anaemia, odynophagia, older onset, vomiting and family cancer history needing urgent endoscopy with imaging for **malignancy**. Rising oesophageal adenocarcinoma on Barrett reflux and squamous disease from smoking with alcohol dominate adult cancer, while Schatzki rings, **Plummer Vinson** webs with iron deficiency, reflux with caustic and radiation strictures, extrinsic compression and immunocompromise candidiasis with odynophagia fill benign differentials.
steps.say: Alarm features are the trigger for urgent endoscopy regardless of age. Progressive sticking with weight loss, anaemia and pain on swallowing is a warning of cancer. Adenocarcinoma on Barrett reflux is rising while smoking with alcohol is a driver of squamous disease. Rings, webs, strictures, compression and candidiasis are the rest of the benign list. Iron deficiency with an upper web points toward Plummer Vinson disease.

steps.tx: Oropharyngeal assessment pairs speech therapy clinical swallow with **videofluoroscopy** or fibreoptic endoscopic evaluation defining aspiration below the cords, silent disease in neurology, penetration and safe consistencies with manoeuvres. Management treats the cause, sets IDDSI **texture** levels, teaches chin tuck or Mendelsohn strategies, and decides oral against **gastrostomy** feeding with patient goals, since thickening helps selected thin fluid aspiration but suits no universal rule.
steps.say: Swallowing assessment is filmed to choose safe textures. Videofluoroscopy with endoscopic evaluation is a revealer of aspiration, penetration and silent events. Speech therapy then sets texture levels with chin tuck or Mendelsohn strategies. The team is weighing oral feeding against gastrostomy with patient goals in view. Thickened fluids help selected patterns but never suit every patient.

steps.tx: Globus means persistent lump sensation between meals without dysphagia, odynophagia or weight loss, often with reflux and hypervigilance, diagnosed after normal examination and indicated scope excludes lesions, then treated with reassurance, reflux measures and speech therapy tension release. Zenker **pharyngeal pouch** through Killian dehiscence in the elderly brings transfer dysphagia with regurgitation of undigested food, halitosis, gurgling swelling and aspiration, confirmed by **barium swallow** toward endoscopic stapling or open surgery, never blind tube or forceful scope that perforates the **pouch**.
steps.say: Globus is a lump sensation between meals without sticking or weight loss. Normal examination with scope where indicated is negative for lesions before reassurance with reflux care. Zenker pouch in the elderly is different with regurgitated undigested food and aspiration. Barium swallow confirms the posterior pouch before stapling or open repair. Blind tubes with forceful scopes are a perforation risk into the pouch.

steps.tx: This lateral barium study shows a posterior **pharyngeal pouch** filling with contrast above a narrowed oesophagus, with arrows at Killian dehiscence, pouch body and retained contrast. The retained sac explains regurgitation of undigested food with halitosis and aspiration in the elderly. Confirm with **barium swallow** before treatment, then favour endoscopic stapling or open surgery while avoiding blind **nasogastric tubes** that enter the pouch.
steps.say: This barium study is a display of the posterior pouch of Zenker disease. Contrast fills a sac above the narrowed gullet with arrows marking the weak spot and the retained column. Retained food explains regurgitation, halitosis and aspiration in older patients. Barium swallow is confirmatory before stapling or open repair. Blind tubes are never put in because the pouch is entered.
